title: Median Salary Per Department Using PERCENTILE_CONT
description:
Calculate the median (50th percentile) salary for each department using the PERCENTILE_CONT ordered-set aggregate function.

**Table: employees** — `id`, `name`, `department`, `salary`

Output columns: `department`, `median_salary`, `avg_salary`. Order by `department`.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE employees (id INT, name VARCHAR, department VARCHAR, salary INT); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'Alice','Engineering',95000),(2,'Bob','Engineering',88000),(3,'Carol','Engineering',72000),(4,'Dave','Engineering',105000),(5,'Eve','Engineering',91000),(6,'Frank','Marketing',65000),(7,'Grace','Marketing',72000),(8,'Henry','Marketing',58000),(9,'Iris','HR',52000),(10,'Jake','HR',60000),(11,'Kim','HR',48000);
solution_sql: SELECT department, PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY salary) AS median_salary, ROUND(AVG(salary), 0) AS avg_salary FROM employees GROUP BY department ORDER BY department

test_cases.description: 3 departments: Engineering (5 employees), Marketing (3), HR (3) — 3 rows with median and average salary

hints: PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY salary) computes the exact 50th percentile using linear interpolation.
Use GROUP BY department to compute the median within each department separately.
explanation: PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY salary) is an ordered-set aggregate. Engineering salaries sorted: 72k,88k,91k,95k,105k → median = 91000 (middle value). Marketing: 58k,65k,72k → median = 65000. HR: 48k,52k,60k → median = 52000. Compare with AVG: medians and averages often differ when there are outliers.
